OmniAPO Guide

Getting from a fresh install to a working setup, and what to do when something is not working. For the exhaustive list of every configuration command, see the Configuration Reference in the same Start Menu group.

No section matches that filter.

What this is

OmniAPO is an Audio Processing Object. Windows loads it inside audiodg.exe and hands it every sample on the way to or from a device. That has two consequences worth understanding before anything else:

  • It affects every application at once — not one player at a time. Browser, game, media player and voice chat all go through the same chain.
  • There is nothing to launch or keep running. If a device is enabled in the Device Selector, OmniAPO is already in its signal path. The Editor is a tool for writing the configuration, not the thing doing the work.

Why the folder still says EqualizerAPO. OmniAPO is a private build of Equalizer APO and deliberately keeps the original install path (C:\Program Files\EqualizerAPO) and registry key. Peace, HeSuVi, OmniEQ and other front ends locate the engine through exactly those, so renaming them would leave every one of those tools unable to find it. The installer does not offer the location as a choice.

First five minutes

  1. Pick your devices. Open the Device Selector (it asks for administrator rights) and tick the playback and recording endpoints OmniAPO should process. Nothing happens on a device that is not ticked.
  2. Confirm it is actually in the path. Open the Configuration Editor. If the registration on a device was lost, it says so here and offers to repair it.
  3. Make one obvious change. In the Editor add a Preamp of -10 dB and save. Music should get quieter within about a second. Undo it. That is the whole feedback loop — edit, save, hear it.
  4. Check your configuration is clean. Use Check configuration in the Start menu, or run Benchmark.exe --check from the install folder. It prints anything the engine rejected, which otherwise only reaches a log file nobody opens.

Before a big edit, copy the config folder somewhere safe. Nothing you write can damage the machine — the worst case is that processing stops — but a copy turns "what did I change?" into a five-second question. The folder is plain text; git init in it works well.

The tools

ToolWhat it is for
Device SelectorChooses which endpoints OmniAPO attaches to. Needs administrator rights, because it writes the APO registration. Changes take effect when the device is next opened.
Configuration EditorWrites the configuration with a live frequency response, a device dropdown and a plugin browser. Everything it can do you can also type by hand; it wins for dialling a curve by ear and for the syntax that is painful to type.
BenchmarkOffline harness. Checks a configuration, or measures what a chain costs, with no audio device involved.
Health AgentVerifies that OmniAPO is still registered for the devices that use it, and offers to repair the registration when it is not. Runs at logon if you kept that component, and on demand from Check registration.

How configurations work

Everything OmniAPO does comes from plain text files in C:\Program Files\EqualizerAPO\config. The engine always starts at config.txt, reads top to bottom, and builds a chain of filters in that order. Save the file and the change is live within about a second — no restart, no toggling the device.

# config.txt - typically nothing but Include: lines
Include: omnieq.txt
Include: HeSuVi\hesuvi.txt

Order is the whole model. A Preamp after a limiter does something different from one before it. And a Channel: line stays in effect until the next one — forgetting to switch back to Channel: all is the single most common mistake.

One file per concern, assembled by config.txt. It keeps diffs readable, lets you disable one concern without unpicking a wall of filters, and — most importantly — means a front end that rewrites its own file can never clobber your handwritten work.

The Configuration Reference documents every command in detail. Start there when you want to know what is possible.

Checking a configuration

The engine reports what it rejected, but only to %TEMP%\EqualizerAPO.log. The checker puts it in front of you instead:

Benchmark.exe --check
Benchmark.exe --check --config D:\configs\test

The second form checks a configuration before you copy it into place. It exits with code 1 if anything was reported, so it works in a script too.

Two things it cannot catch, because the engine does not report them either: a misspelled command name is dropped in silence, and a bare whole number in Copy: selects a channel rather than setting a gain. If a line seems to be ignored and the checker is quiet, check the spelling first.

Adding plugins

OmniAPO hosts VST2 and VST3 effects in the same chain as its own filters. Plugins must be 64-bit.

VST3Plugin: Library LoudMax.vst3
VST3Plugin: Library "C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3\Airwindows Consolidated.vst3" CID {...}

Let the Editor write these lines. It lists the effect classes inside a module, shows the plugin's own interface, and emits the correct CID plus a saved state. Typing a GUID and a base64 blob by hand is not a good use of an evening.

Latency is compensated automatically. One boundary worth knowing: if a plugin changes its latency while running — LoudMax's ISP switch, for example — the new value is picked up at the next configuration reload, not mid-stream. Re-save the file after toggling such an option.

A plugin that crashes is disabled rather than being allowed to take audiodg.exe down with it. That is a safety net, not a licence to run unstable plugins — test new ones at low volume.

Peace, HeSuVi and OmniEQ

These write configuration files for you. They keep working with OmniAPO because the install path, registry key and file format are unchanged — that is the whole reason those were left alone.

Decide which file each tool owns. If two tools write the same file, one will overwrite the other's work without warning. Give each its own file and reference it from config.txt with a single Include: line. This is the most common way people lose an afternoon's tuning.

A useful pattern is a final safety limiter placed after every Include:, so it catches whatever any front end leaves on the bus:

# last line of config.txt
VST3Plugin: Library LoudMax.vst3

Nothing is happening

In rough order of likelihood:

  1. The device is not ticked in the Device Selector — or the one that is ticked is not the one Windows is actually using. Endpoints with similar names are easy to confuse.
  2. The registration was lost. Open the Editor; it detects this and offers a repair. A Windows feature update is the usual cause.
  3. A Device: or Stage: line above your edit excludes the current device, so the whole block is skipped.
  4. An earlier Channel: line is still narrowing the selection to a couple of channels.
  5. The file is not actually reached by an Include: chain from config.txt.
  6. The line was rejected. Run Benchmark.exe --check.

Self-repair

Windows feature updates sometimes wipe the APO registration from an endpoint. Audio keeps playing, so nothing looks broken — your configuration simply stops applying.

OmniAPO detects this and offers a one-click repair. It asks first and never repairs silently. Two places trigger the check:

  • At logon, through the background task.
  • When the Editor starts.

The background task is a component you can decline at install time, listed as Registration self-repair. Declining it means the check only runs when the Editor starts, not at logon. If you skipped it and want it back, run HealthAgent.exe -i from the install folder.

You can also run the check yourself at any time — Check registration in the Start menu, or HealthAgent.exe with no arguments. Started by hand it answers either way, including telling you that everything is in order.

OmniAPO never contacts a server. There is no update check, no version ping and no telemetry of any kind; the binaries link no networking library at all. New versions are downloaded and installed by hand.

Removed or unplugged hardware is deliberately not reported — otherwise every disconnected headset would raise a false alarm.

Other symptoms

Distortion or crackling

Almost always clipping from positive gain. Add or lower a Preamp until it stops. The rule of thumb is one Preamp near the top of the chain set to the negative of your largest boost.

A microphone went silent

The old bug behind this is fixed in this build. If it still happens, toggle the device off and on in the Device Selector and check whether a Stage: capture block is doing something unintended.

A plugin does not load

It must be 64-bit. Quote paths containing spaces. For a module with several effects, give a CID — without one you get the first class, which may not be the one you want.

Starting over

An empty config.txt is a valid, fully bypassed configuration. Rename your files aside rather than deleting them, confirm clean audio, then add them back one Include: at a time.

What this build adds

Compared with stock Equalizer APO:

  • VST3 plugin hosting alongside the existing VST2 support, with class selection by GUID, state persistence and latency compensation.
  • Renaming a device no longer breaks its configuration — a Device: line carrying a matching endpoint GUID matches regardless of the name words.
  • Disabling effects no longer silences capture devices whose input and output channel counts differ.
  • Device names with illegal filename characters no longer break installation.
  • Self-repair for a wiped APO registration.
  • A configuration checker and this offline documentation.

The build is compiled for AVX2 with 64-bit double-precision processing throughout.

Where everything lives

PathWhat it is
C:\Program Files\EqualizerAPO\config\Every file the engine reads.
config\config.txtThe root file. The engine always starts here.
VSTPlugins\Default folder for relative plugin paths.
docs\This guide, the README and the Configuration Reference.
licenses\Full licence text for every bundled component.
%TEMP%\EqualizerAPO.logThe engine's log. --check reads the same diagnostics.
